lines.say: Sixty two percent of Israeli women are in the workforce, working or looking for work. Is that a lot?

lines.screen: Women in the labour force, *1990* to 2024

lines.say: In 1990, America leads with fifty six percent. Britain is next. Israel, forty six.
Then Israeli women keep joining. In 2001, Israel passes Britain.
Saudi Arabia climbs from fifteen percent to thirty three, most of it after 2017.
Egypt, Jordan, Iran and Syria are still under one in five.
lines.screen: Egypt, Jordan, Iran, Syria: under *1 in 5*

lines.say: The UAE nearly doubles, from twenty nine to fifty three. Turkey reaches thirty seven.
Germany starts just behind Israel, and ends at fifty six.
What gets more women into work? Tell me in the comments.

end.balance: Working is one measure. *Pay gaps* exist everywhere.

caption_en:
In 1990 this country was third. Watch who it passes.

Women in the labour force, % of women aged 15+ (ILO modelled estimates via the World Bank, 2024):
Israel 62.2%
UK 57.5%
USA 56.6%
Germany 55.6%
UAE 52.5%
Turkey 36.8%
Saudi Arabia 33.3%
Lebanon 22.2% (2023, latest)
Egypt 18.5%
Jordan 16.0%
Iran 14.1%
Syria 12.8%

1990: USA 56.0%, UK 52.0%, Israel 46.3%. Israel passed the UK in 2001 and the USA in 2011. Saudi Arabia rose from 15.0% (1990) and 19.9% (2017) to 33.3% (2024).
The labour force counts women working or looking for work. It says nothing about pay, and pay gaps exist in every country here.

Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators, SL.TLF.CACT.FE.ZS (ILO modelled estimates), 1990 to 2024. The animation interpolates between years.

caption_he: 62% מהנשים בישראל בכוח העבודה (ILO דרך הבנק העולמי, 2024), הכי הרבה מבין 12 המדינות, לפני בריטניה (57.5%) וארה"ב (56.6%). ב 1990 ישראל הייתה שלישית. סעודיה קפצה מ 15% ל 33%.
